fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Internet as a One-Person Newsroom", "body": "Chance recalls studying journalism, hating it and failing out, yet argues that grassroots journalism matters more now than ever. James, an English literature graduate who became a teacher in Japan and then a journalist of sorts online, says the way he works would have been unthinkable a decade ago. His example: while researching eugenics he read about a Chicago doctor of that era who made a silent film about his own story, typed The Black Stork into YouTube and watched it. James says ordinary people now hold more data than emperors ever dreamed of, and that information overload is an opportunity if we make something of it."}, {"title": "Gateway to the Rabbit Hole", "body": "James calls 9/11 his gateway into conspiracy research. He started watching early YouTube documentaries half expecting to debunk them, checked the claims one by one, and found that enough details held up to convince him there was more to the story. He also credits temperament, a lifelong refusal to accept dumbed down answers, recalling a fourth grade science class where getting the right answer was not enough for him without knowing why. Chance points listeners to James's interview on the plot to kill Martin Luther King, and James says the decades of documented research behind it left him certain that James Earl Ray was not the killer."}, {"title": "Reaching People Who Resist", "body": "Asked how to reach friends and family who push back, James says there is no single answer because everyone has a different blind spot; he read the 9/11 Commission Report when it came out and did not question it until 2006. His advice is to plant seeds, speak with confidence rather than neediness, and talk to a person rather than at them. He urges humility about what we do not yet know and wants the strongest opposing arguments, noting that his Federal Reserve documentary deliberately quotes the Fed's own words. Both men credit literary training, and James says documentary making comes back to writing an essay."}, {"title": "Beyond a Clockwork Universe", "body": "Asked for his cosmology, James says he is not a materialist, and draws on Heidegger's The Question Concerning Technology to describe how a purely measuring mindset turns the world into resources to be used. If he believed he were a biological robot in a meaningless universe, he says, hedonism would be the only sensible philosophy, so care for the human spirit is what drives his work. Chance points to neuroplasticity as evidence that thought changes the brain. James then argues that psychopaths in power have to play on ordinary people's empathy, citing the boy in the Syrian ambulance and the intervention in Libya, and finds hope in that empathy."}, {"title": "Decentralization as the Real Revolution", "body": "Chance asks what can be done about psychopaths in positions of power. James says psychopathy alone does not make a ruler, it takes a cluster of traits like the dark triad, and the real danger is centralized power that lets such people harm millions. His answer is decentralization: he sees the nineteenth century fight over the means of production as dated when his own computer is his means of production and 3D printing may soon put manufacturing on the desktop, whatever DRM the powerful try to impose. Chance adds doing no harm and growing gardens, and James closes by urging listeners to be conscious actors, not spectators."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: James Corbett is a voice for independent journalism and truth-based internet media who hosts a website and Youtube channel called The Corbett Report. Join us for a conversation about our experiences with seeking and sharing the deeper truths that are required for humanity to realize... if we're going to survive on this planet together for much longer, that is. It's a high energy interview where we touch only many different topics, especially conspiracy facts and the truth-seeker's crusade to wake up the sheeple!
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: The immeasurable power of the average person's ability to access and share information
